_comment: Adding a row is a ruling. A row names a program whose both-stop a test already holds: the JavaScript backend and native stop alike, exit 70, with the same stdout and stderr, where Node runs the program to the end, exit 0. The agreement mode of cmd/adamic-admission-delta counts such a program as a checked stop, not as a disagreement, only when its path is listed here and the backends' stderr is the row's byte for byte. A row is itself the pin of the stop's words (Adamic on #d358hc1), and only a hatch may stop a valid program loudly, so a program with no hatch in it is never a row. Schema: stops is an array of rows, each with path (the program's repository path, listed once), stderr (the backends' exact stderr, the run's checkout written {root}), hatch (the hatch the program uses, as <kind>[ (<detail>)], line <n>: <that line of the program, trimmed>, a language hatch's detail citing docs/rulings.md:<line>, "<the row's opening words>") and test (the test that holds the stop, as <repository path>_test.go: <TestName>). A row without its hatch or its test is refused, and TestHeldStopListHoldsItsRows holds each row's hatch line, ruling and test to the tree.
